target_customer: Pakistani micro and small retailers (kiryana, mobile shops, distributors, pharmacies), about 30M micro SMEs per YC
problem: Small businesses in Pakistan track credit (udhaar) and cash in paper ledgers.
business_model: Free bookkeeping app monetized via commissions on mobile top-ups, bill payments and vouchers (site: up to 2% and 4%)
product_category: SMB bookkeeping and payments super-app (khata app)

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile bookkeeping app; payments integrations add some complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Ledger data creates mild lock-in, but khata apps are copyable.

market_need_then: Millions of small businesses use paper khata; company later claims 5.1M businesses on the app (self-reported, 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, merchant-focused; 'One app to scale your entire business'

brand_strength.rationale: The Urdu word for credit is native to the exact use case, but no brand press seen.

outcome_analysis: Udhaar Book is Active with 32 people and, by its own claim, 5.1 million businesses, which would indicate real traction in a large Pakistani small-business market. A Bloomberg headline of 2021-11-08 reports a raise, but the amount and investors were not accessible, so the funding story is incomplete.
notes: Bloomberg article (2021-11-08, 'Udhaar Book Raises Funds to Digitize Pakistan's Retail Shops') returned 403; amount unknown so no round recorded. The 'udhaar' term meaning is inferred from the site's usage (credit), not an origin statement.
